Metadata.GlobalAvailability: DermGPT is available for dermatologists to use at no cost [SOURCE 3].
Metadata.Summary: DermGPT is an AI chatbot designed to streamline clinical tasks, improve access to dermatologic data, and save time for physicians. It is built on over 3,000 peer-reviewed articles and allows dermatologists to ask questions in natural language and receive relevant answers [SOURCE 3, 4].
Metadata.Keywords: AI; artificial intelligence; dermatology; chatbot; clinical efficiency; prior authorizations; patient education; telehealth

UsesAndDirections.IntendedUseAndWorkflow: DermGPT is intended to assist with tasks such as providing quick references for medication options, summarizing diagnosis and treatment guidelines, suggesting labs and procedures, automating documentation, answering diagnostic questions, writing insurance authorization letters, and creating patient handouts [SOURCE 4]. It can be used by physicians, RNs, MAs, and ancillary staff during the clinical day to quickly look up information, answer patient questions, and access handouts [SOURCE 4].
UsesAndDirections.PrimaryIntendedUsers: The primary intended users are dermatologists, dermatology providers, RNs, MAs, and ancillary staff [SOURCE 4].
UsesAndDirections.NecessaryKnowledgeExpertise: Users should have knowledge and expertise in dermatology to complement DermGPT's data-driven tasks with human creativity, intuition, and problem-solving skills. DermGPT is designed to assist, not replace, medical decision-making [SOURCE 4].
UsesAndDirections.HowToUse: Dermatologists can sign up at dermgpt.com and start using the chatbot clinically for free. They can ask questions in natural language and receive relevant, helpful answers [SOURCE 3, 4]. The platform is designed to be intuitive and user-friendly with clear navigation [SOURCE 4].
UsesAndDirections.TargetedPatientPopulation: DermGPT is intended to improve patient care by streamlining dermatology practices, assisting with clinical tasks, and making dermatology information readily available [SOURCE 4]. It also aims to improve access to new therapies for patients [SOURCE 3].

Warnings.DeveloperSuppliedWarnings: DermGPT should not be used as a stand-alone decision maker, but as an assistant. It is not a human and lacks human creativity and intuition. It excels in efficient and data-driven tasks [SOURCE 4].
Warnings.ModelLimitations: The AI tool excels in efficient and data-driven tasks but lacks human creativity, intuition, and the ability to think outside the box. It is most powerful when paired with a dermatology provider or staff who can complement its skills with their higher-level creative problem-solving. [SOURCE 4]

TrustIngredients.AISystemFacts: DermGPT is an AI chatbot built on more than 3,000 peer-reviewed articles. It is designed to provide more specific and reliable answers to dermatology-related questions, minimizing errors found in generic language models. It can be used for prior authorizations, denial letters, resident board study, and patient education handouts. [SOURCE 3]
TrustIngredients.InteractionWithOtherSystems: DermGPT can integrate with existing EHR systems to streamline documentation and facilitate seamless information exchange. [SOURCE 4]
TrustIngredients.OutcomesAndOutput: DermGPT can provide healthcare providers with quick references for medication options, dosing, and interactions; summarize diagnosis and treatment guidelines for complex cases; suggest appropriate labs, imaging, and procedures for diagnostic workups; automate documentation such as visit notes, orders, and prescriptions; write insurance authorization letters; and create patient handouts. [SOURCE 4]
TrustIngredients.TypeAndValueOfSolutionOutput: DermGPT provides information including diagnoses, treatments, and prior authorization criteria. It assists with patient management and shared decision-making tools such as patient educational handouts and prescription programs. [SOURCE 4]
TrustIngredients.ExplanationForHowAnOutputIsGenerated: DermGPT pulls information from a proprietary database of trusted, physician-approved sources and peer-reviewed medical journals. [SOURCE 4]
